items.name: Strive
items.headline: Bitcoin funding plans meet the execution test
items.fact: The Block reported that Strive's CEO discussed potential funding from warrants expiring in October. The larger Bitcoin accumulation scenario was conditional, not his base case.
items.bullCase: Additional capital could support Bitcoin purchases if warrant holders exercise. That is a possible outcome, not completed funding.
items.watchFor: Check company filings for actual warrant exercises and Bitcoin per share. Separate completed purchases from management targets.
items.risk: New shares can dilute existing holders. Bitcoin can fall, and potential warrant proceeds are not guaranteed.

items.name: Hafnia Limited
items.headline: Strong results, but watch the next freight rates
items.fact: Hafnia reported Q2 net profit of $277.8 million, versus $75.3 million a year earlier. Profit included $39.3 million from vessel sales.
items.bullCase: Stronger earnings and a lower debt-to-vessel-value ratio support the company's financial position.
items.watchFor: Compare the next fleet booking update with Q2. Rates already booked for 80% of Q3 earning days averaged $30,716 per day, below Q2's $44,093.
items.risk: Tanker rates are cyclical. Lower rates and non-recurring vessel-sale gains mean Q2 profit is not a promise of future earnings or dividends.
